newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria and S.Africa agree on steps to spur trade.
newsitem.headline: Algeria and S.Africa agree on steps to spur trade.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki on Sunday agreed with Algerian Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia on steps to boost cooperation and trade links, the official Algerian news agency APS said.

"The two delegations reasserted their determination to reinforce and consolidate links of friendship and cooperation existing between the two countries," Mbeki and Ouyahia said in a joint statement carried by APS.
They agreed to set up a joint cooperation committee and work on finalising agreements of interest to both sides, it said.
The South African deputy head of state announced that his government would open an embassy soon in Algiers, which will be a vehicle to boost links and trade, APS said.
He held talks with President Liamine Zeroual and several other Algerian leaders before leaving Algiers on Sunday at the end of a three-day visit.

Mbeki, who is almost certain to suceed President Nelson Mandela in 1999, visited Tunisia earlier in the week and is expected on Sunday in Mali. His trip is focused on developing diplomatic and trade relations with the three countries.
